scope: Shared-backend measurements from the local development bundle 1.1.0; not a real-audio run of either English 0.2.0 bundle identity.

checks: Real AudioEngine.refresh/completion ran through >3-second watchdog intervals
A stopped real I/O for >4 seconds without a connection error
A resumed automatically; B retained 75% emitted gain
New A process retained stable app ID and 25% setting
Active nonempty A topology swap preserved the same tap/aggregate and sustained A=25%, B=75%
Muting A emits silence while B retains 75%
Unmuting and changing both gains emits A=50%, B=30%
No new audio taps remained after shutdown
Default output UID, sample rate, master/channel scalar and mute unchanged
Every observed transport had valid capture/render rates and AUHAL physical input I/O disabled
Read-only default input UID, sample rate and supported input master/channel volume/mute controls unchanged
Real Chrome produces a stable native signal
Real Chrome connects through production AudioEngine worker
Independent replay capture matches Chrome native baseline at 50%, 25%, 150%, 200% and mute for a low-level signal
Real Chrome sustained 50% independent replay for at least 60 seconds with physical input I/O disabled
Worker cleanup acknowledged and process exited; monitor destroy calls succeeded; default output unchanged

limitations: Digital measurements do not establish acoustic loudness or what a remote participant hears.
The English bundles have different permissions identities and require their own real-audio run.
A short repeat launch initially failed to discover its helper within two seconds; bounded helper startup was extended to eight seconds before this successful sustained run.
Underflow counters increased during the run; the check establishes gain and bounded connection behavior, not glitch-free playback.
Real calls, conferencing AEC/AGC, Bluetooth, Intel and broad OS/device compatibility are unvalidated.
